name: Domaine Gourt de Mautens (Jérôme Bressy) Vaucluse Rouge 2012
text:
## Domaine Gourt de Mautens (Jérôme Bressy) Vaucluse Rouge 2012

**The story.** Jérôme Bressy created Domaine Gourt de Mautens in [Rasteau](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Domaine+Gourt+de+Mautens,+Rasteau,+France&t=k) in 1996, when he was barely 23. Rasteau was then a fairly obscure Côtes-du-Rhône village, known mostly for its [vin doux naturel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vin_doux_naturel), a fortified sweet wine. With his family's old, naturally low-yielding vines, Bressy burst onto the scene and, with André Roméro of Domaine la Soumade, showed what Rasteau's terroirs could do. His father, Yves Bressy, had converted the vineyards to organic farming in 1989, so he started with healthy vines and living soils; in 2008 he completed the move to [biodynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biodynamic_agriculture), certified by [Demeter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demeter_International) (an importer's text quoted in a [Wine Berserkers offer](https://www.wineberserkers.com/t/southern-rhone-fans-supplier-closeout-deal/147797)).

**Why "Vaucluse" and not Rasteau?** In 2012 the wine was labelled only as IGP [Vaucluse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaucluse), a humbler category, because the blend held a high share of old Rhône grapes: Vaccarèse, [Counoise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counoise), [Carignan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carignan), [Cinsault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinsaut) and Terret Noir. The Rasteau rules then allowed these grapes only up to 15%, so Bressy gave up the appellation rather than change his vineyard ([Wine Berserkers offer](https://www.wineberserkers.com/t/southern-rhone-fans-supplier-closeout-deal/147797)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [southern Rhône vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/southern-rhone) calls 2012 much more successful than 2011: a low-acid year with roughly average alcohol and volumes down by up to 15%, but clement weather late in the season made for relaxed picking, and the wines combine ripeness with some freshness. "Most look set to peak in their teenage years."

**What the critics say for 2012.**
- **[Jeb Dunnuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeb_Dunnuck), [Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 95** (as quoted in the [Wine Berserkers offer](https://www.wineberserkers.com/t/southern-rhone-fans-supplier-closeout-deal/147797)). "A true blockbuster": Grenache-dominated, all from clay and limestone soils around Rasteau, aged 24 to 36 months in foudres and demi-muids. Black cherries, black currants, crushed rocks, licorice and roasted herbs; full-bodied, "voluptuous, sexy and gorgeously textured", with notable purity, good freshness and ripe tannin. "It will continue to knock your socks off for another 10-15 years."
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 90.5** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is fourteen years old: the "teenage years" Jancis Robinson predicted for the vintage's peak. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2021 to 2031. So it is in its prime now. Decant it for an hour, mainly to leave the sediment behind, and serve at 16 to 18°C.

**Food.** Provençal daube of beef, roast lamb with garlic and herbs, or game birds.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Gourt de Mautens at the moment.

**Curious details**
- **Waiting for the rules.** Bressy planned to stay with the humbler label until the Rasteau rules caught up, which the offer expected in 2019 ([Wine Berserkers offer](https://www.wineberserkers.com/t/southern-rhone-fans-supplier-closeout-deal/147797)).

- [Jancis Robinson, southern Rhône vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/southern-rhone)
